title: Loop Engineering: From Prompts to Bounded Autonomy

questions.question: What must a goal loop have before it can safely run without a person prompting every turn?
options: A goal, an independent evaluator, and explicit stop conditions
A larger model and a longer prompt
A timer with no maximum duration
A second chat window that repeats the same request
questions.explanation: The loop contract is the goal, machine-checkable evidence from an evaluator, and bounded exits. More prompting does not create a stopping policy.

questions.question: Which role owns the completion decision in the maker/evaluator design?
options: The maker, because it knows what it intended
The evaluator, using structured evidence against the goal
The timer, because elapsed time proves progress
The human only, even when the loop is unattended
questions.explanation: The maker produces an artifact; the independent evaluator decides whether the artifact satisfies the contract.

questions.question: Why does the reference loop stop on a stalled artifact?
options: Repeated unchanged failures are evidence that another round is unlikely to help
A loop may never inspect the same artifact twice
Stalls mean the evaluator has passed
The maker is allowed only one call
questions.explanation: A stall guard limits unattended waste and escalates when the maker is not changing a failing artifact.

questions.question: Which trigger is the honest default for a check that has no natural finish line?
options: Goal trigger
Timer or event trigger with idempotency and retry limits
Manual trigger with hidden retries
An infinite goal loop
questions.explanation: Timer and event loops handle recurring or reactive work; a goal loop needs a verifiable end state.

questions.question: What should every non-success loop exit provide to the next session?
options: A claim that the agent nearly finished
Only the final artifact, without failed attempts
A status, reason, round receipts, and an escalation or next action
A larger model selection
questions.explanation: A bounded stop is useful only when its evidence can be reviewed and resumed, not when it disappears into chat.

questions.question: What is the safest way to automate an irreversible production action?
options: Put it behind the maker and let the maker approve itself
Run it on a timer first and inspect only failures
Define evaluator evidence, scope, approval, and rollback before enabling the side effect
Remove the round budget so it can retry until it works
questions.explanation: Irreversible work needs an independent gate and an operator recovery path before autonomy is expanded.
